symptom: Source-filtered SB3 distillation could learn from 424 clean parent late-state risk recovery samples while preserving offline anchor alignment, but no tested risk weight produced an acceptable 300s high-pressure policy. w10 restored a cracked-star-jar 300s win rate of 0.3333 but caused severe e30 and parent window regressions; w7 and w5 reduced regressions but returned to 0.0/0.0/0.0 300s win rates.
root_cause: The clean risk rows expose useful late action-separation signal, but applying them as a global supervised distillation weight shifts shared policy behavior across maps and phases. Higher weights create local cracked-star-jar conversion at the cost of soda-creek and caramel-workshop retention, while lower weights are too weak to create terminal conversion.
fix: Reject all sweep candidates as policy candidates. Keep the source-filtered distillation tooling, but move the next repair to map/phase-scoped objectives that preserve soda-creek opening/mid and caramel-workshop 180s behavior while applying clean risk rows only to matching late failure states.
validation: w10 source-filtered distillation passed drift and full-anchor alignment, but comparison_300s.json was 0.0/0.0/0.3333 and repair_probe_gate.json failed with 14 blockers. w7 and w5 passed drift/full-anchor alignment and reduced blockers to 3 and 4 respectively, but both comparison_300s.json reports remained 0.0/0.0/0.0. failure_analysis_300s.json recorded 8 failures for w10 and 9 failures for w7/w5.
